excerpt:
**CITY OF AURORA  
 REFERENDUM**(DuPage, Kane, Kendall, & Will Counties)  
  
 AURORA MAYOR RECALL PROCEDURE  

_Shall the City of Aurora adopt the following electoral system immediately upon passage of this binding referendum: the Mayor may be recalled and removed by a majority vote at a recall election that may be triggered by the filing of a recall petition signed by a number of Aurora electors equal to 20% of the total votes cast for all candidates for mayor in the immediately preceding mayoral election; and upon the certification of a valid recall petition, the question “Shall (name of Mayor) be recalled and removed from the Office of Mayor of the City of Aurora” shall be placed on the ballot at the immediately succeeding regularly-scheduled election to be held in the City of Aurora; and that in the event the Mayor is recalled and removed, the City Council shall fill the vacancy in the office of Mayor within 30 days from the date of the recall election, which appointment shall be for the remainder of the term, except that if more than 13 months remain in the term, the City Council shall set a date for a special election to be held within 9 months of the recall election at which time the voters of the City of Aurora shall elect a Mayor to serve the remaining term in office?_

**RICHLAND SCHOOL DISTRICT 88A**  
**REFERENDUM**PROPOSITION TO INCREASE THE LIMITING RATE
_Shall the limiting rate under the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law for Richland School District Number 88A, Will County, Illinois, be increased by an additional amount equal to 0.3900% above the limiting rate for levy year 2025 for school purposes, and be equal to 2.7833% of the equalized assessed value of the taxable property therein for levy year 2026?_

_(1) The approximate amount of taxes extendable at the most recently extended limiting rate is $10,891,203 and the approximate amount of taxes extendable if the proposition is approved is $12,665,978._

_(2) For the 2026 levy year the approximate amount of the additional tax extendable against property containing a single family residence and having a fair market value at the time of the referendum of $100,000 is estimated to be $130.00._

_(3) If the proposition is approved, the aggregate extension for 2026 will be determined by the limiting rate set forth in the proposition, rather than the otherwise applicable limiting rate calculated under the provisions of the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law (commonly known as the Property Tax Cap Law)._
